text: A tall black hat drops onto a Pilgrim, with a big shiny buckle on the front. It's the Thanksgiving look everyone knows.
Except the Pilgrims never dressed like that.
When a Pilgrim died, everything they owned was written down, item by item.
Elder William Brewster's list had a violet coat, green pants, a blue suit, and a red cap.
No buckles. Those weren't common until much later.
Black was one of the priciest dyes, so it was saved for Sundays and paintings.
The buckles came from artists in the 1800s, who wanted the Pilgrims to look old-fashioned.
It's the same trick they used on Santa Claus. That's why he has buckles too.
Happy Thanksgiving. Follow for more history myths.
